newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil steady to a shade softer.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil steady to a shade softer.

text.p: The European low sulphur straight-run market was thinkly talked a shade softer on Wednesday, as buyers started to lower their bids, traders said.
Buyers and sellers were far apart in the mid to high nineties and low $100s respectively but the low buying interest was met with thin supply.
One seller said it was willing to sell its end month cargo for $100 a tonne, or some $1 lower than its pervious asking price, adding it was not actively marketing it.
A buyer said he would consider picking it or a second cargo on offer at about $97/$98.
Sellers of better quality material were around the $103/$104 mark.
"I don't think any deals were done at all this week. Sellers are tying for three figures but no buyer is going to do that," one trader said.
However, some traders said that with crude seemingly bottoming out, low sulphur straight-run could pick up soon.
